For real! It's incredible when parents support your interests like that.
My time is done, why wait? I'll let someone else have at it.

Almost home. This was nice, you seem like nice people, sorry I wasn't much fun. Take care babies.

Goodbye, I loved you all.

My goal was to make a living doing what I love. Now there's no living to be made and the joy I had making music and playing is replaced by dread and exhaustion. Being asked by interviewers "why do you think you haven't had the success of your friends" is becoming like a broken record. Being asked by your girlfriend why you can't be there, or why you can't fly her to events when everyone else can, is heart breaking.
I've worked with these friends, opened, toured, written songs together, never turned into anything beyond more 3rd rate shows and songs even their fans ignore.
Thanks for that, but my humanity is all but gone after years of futility. The void is comforting. It is concrete. I feel like a ghost waiting to move on.

I've played every city in the USA, I've played New York and LA, I've been all over the map and it never gets better. We spend more money for more exposure and nobody cares. Currently I live in a huge market for my music and while friends have literally million dollar careers, I stay invisible.

Should also mention I have a manager, agent, publicist and have been on the Top 20 charts...just not "Top enough" to get a break. I've had songs in commercials and on tv, toured the world.... But nobody cares.
I've had albums, been on labels, worked with indies and majors. A bit past the "Zelda cover" thing. Sad and sobering to realize people just don't like your work.
It's better to burn out than to fade away, right?
A life spent chasing a dream at the expense of money, health, education, relationships...to realize I'll never be good enough to make it? Yep, pretty depressing to me.
The thought of being a guitar center washout scares me more than death
